name: Lunar Roving Vehicle
description: The Lunar Roving Vehicle was a battery-powered exploration vehicle. Apollo 15 first used it in 1971, followed by Apollo 16 and Apollo 17 in 1972. Their rovers stayed on the lunar surface after each crew departed.
function: Carry two suited astronauts, tools and samples across terrain beyond practical walking range.
importance: The Apollo 17 rover traveled 30.5 km across three excursions, extending the reach of geological fieldwork. Its TV camera filmed Challenger’s ascent from the final parking area.
placement: Apollo 17’s final parking position is separately labelled LRV in the NASA LRO image of the landing site.

name: Lunar Module Descent Stage
description: The lower stage of Challenger housed the descent engine, landing gear and surface equipment. It supported the crew’s landing and provided the platform from which the ascent stage lifted off.
function: Control powered descent, absorb landing loads and support surface operations.
importance: The remaining stage marks the Apollo 17 landing site and helps anchor later observations of the crew’s activities.
placement: NASA’s Apollo 17 mission summary gives the Challenger landing point as 20.19080° N, 30.77168° E.

sources.title: NASA Science · Orbital image of Apollo 17

name: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package
description: ALSEP was a group of instruments and a central station deployed by Apollo crews. The Apollo 17 station measured properties of the Moon and its local environment.
function: Support surface science including measurements related to heat flow, the lunar atmosphere and seismic activity.
importance: Surface instruments collected observations independently of the crew’s presence and expanded the scientific return of the landing.
placement: The Apollo 17 crew deployed the ALSEP about 185 m west-northwest of Challenger, according to NASA’s mission summary.
